𝐄𝐥𝐲𝐬𝐢𝐮𝐦, 𝟐𝟎𝟏𝟑.⁣
⁣
Set in 2154, Elysium imagines a future where Earth has become overcrowded, polluted and dominated by poverty. The wealthiest people have abandoned the planet entirely, living instead on Elysium, a luxurious space station with advanced technology capable of curing almost any disease.⁣
⁣
What makes Elysium interesting is how believable parts of this future feel. There is essentially no middle class anymore: society has been divided between those who have everything and those struggling to survive. Earth is filled with broken infrastructure and outdated equipment, yet incredibly advanced technology still exists for corporations, security forces and the wealthy.⁣
⁣
Matt Damon plays Max, a factory worker who is exposed to a lethal dose of radiation and discovers that his only chance of survival is reaching Elysium. His mission gradually becomes something much bigger, putting him against government officials, corporations and Sharlto Copley’s brutal mercenary Kruger.⁣
⁣
The contrast between both worlds is one of the movie’s strongest ideas. Elysium looks like paradise, but the people living there aren’t necessarily smarter or more capable. Their society still suffers from corruption, bureaucracy and political power struggles. Meanwhile, the people left on Earth survive through friendship, resilience and whatever technology they can piece together.⁣
⁣
Director Neill Blomkamp combines this social commentary with cyberpunk technology, robots, hackers, body modifications and large-scale action. The visual effects still hold up remarkably well, while Damon gives the madness around him a grounded center. ⁣
⁣
Rate 𝐄𝐥𝐲𝐬𝐢𝐮𝐦 (𝟐𝟎𝟏𝟑) out of ten.⁣

source_details.synopsis: Elysium is a 2013 American dystopian science fiction action film written, co-produced, and directed by Neill Blomkamp. It was Blomkamp's second directorial effort. The film stars Matt Damon and Jodie Foster alongside Sharlto Copley, Alice Braga, Diego Luna, Wagner Moura, and William Fichtner. It takes place on a ravaged Earth and a luxurious artificial world called Elysium. The film offers deliberate social commentary. The film was released on August 9, 2013, by Sony Pictures Releasing through the TriStar Pictures label, in both conventional and IMAX theaters.
